Name: Pre-diagnosis
Description: - Patient goes for tests, and mammogram, Ultrasound, US and biopsy. It can be either of the following- Mammogram + Biopsy, or US + biopsy or MMG+US_Biopsy

Name: Results Clinic
Patient Facing Questions:
Have you been told what treatments? 
If yes, are you having chemotherapy, hormone tablets or surgery? DO NO PRESENT but identify from OTHER- other option here are palliative and in rare cases radiotherapy
Description: Patient is given diagnosis for the first time. This is a very sensitive step as the patient is hearing the news for the first time

Name: palliative
Description: Metastasis has happened and hence curative treatment is not possible.

Name: primary endocrine
Patient Facing Label: My first treatment is Hormone Tablets
Description:
endocrine (anti hormone medication) as first line treatment. 
There are multiple reasons for choosing this treatment path, the most common one being patient may not be fit for surgery.
Transition notes from this stage to next: Hormone therapy is effective on the patient

Name: Follow-up Clinic
Description: follow up to see if hormone treatment is working with a Specialist Clinician (this is not same as results clinic)

Name: Continue same endocrine treatment
Description: If, on follow up, cancer is reducing in size, then you are okay to continue on same medication.

Name: Change to another medication
Description: If, on follow up, cancer is getting bigger, then doctors will put you on another anti hormone medication, or discuss surgery with you (see stage 2)

Name: Further investigation
Description: Following review of previous work up in the MDM, patient is reviewed in results clinic  to discuss next step, which could be either to start treatment or for further investigation,

Name: Surgery
Patient Facing Questions: Have you been described what type of surgery - Breast Surgery or Armpit or Both?
Description: Master Stage for various surgery types. The patient may go through some of the surgeries in the steps 2.1 or 2.2 etc. and end up in a post surgery MDM where the next steps are defined.

Name: Breast surgery
Description: Operations on the breast to remove cancer and, when possible, preserve appearance and function.

Name: Breast Conservation Surgery
Patient Facing Questions:
Is your surgery to remove the tumor only and not the whole breast? or - 
Option 1. Remove the tumor (Lumpectomy)
Option 2: Remove tumor (Lumpectomy) and remove and reduce the breast (Therapeutic mammaplasty)
Option 3: Remove the tumor (Lumpectomy) and fill the defect with skin and fat from chest wall (Chest wall perforator flap)
Description: Operations which remove the cancer while keeping most of the breast, almost always followed by radiotherapy.

Name: Wide local excision
Description: Operation to remove the cancer with a margin of healthy tissue, keeping the rest of the breast, when the cancer to breast size ratio allows (for example, small cancer in large breast).

Name: Oncoplastic Breast Conservation Surgery
Description: Operations which combine cancer removal with plastic surgery techniques to improve breast shape.

Name: Therapeutic mammaplasty/mammoplasty
Description: Operation which combines cancer removal with breast-reduction techniques, allowing removal of bigger cancer from big/droopy breast. This may or may not be combined with reduction of the other breast to symmetrize.

Name: Chest wall perforator flap
Description: Operation which combines cancer removal and use of nearby skin and fat to fill the defect after cancer removal, allowing removal of bigger cancer from small breast.

Name: Mastectomy
Patient Facing Questions:
Is your surgery to remove whole breast? or - 
Option 1. Remove the breast (Mastectomy)
Option 2: Remove breast (Mastectomy) and reconstruction with implant
Option 3: Remove breast (Mastectomy) and reconstruction with own tissue (autologous)
Description: Operations which remove all the breast tissue, including the cancer.

Name: Simple mastectomy no reconstruction
Description: Operation which removes all the breast tissue, including the cancer, without rebuilding (going flat chest, with scar).

Name: Mastectomy and reconstruction
Description: Operation which removes all the breast tissue, including the cancer, and rebuilds the breast mound.

Name: Autologous reconstruction
Description: Breast rebuilt using your own tissue from another body area.

Name: Implant based reconstruction
Description: Breast rebuilt using a silicone or saline implant.

Name: Axillary surgery
Patient Facing Questions:
Is your surgery on armpit? or - 
Option 1: Only a few lymph glands being removed (sentinel lymph node biopsy)
Option 2: All lymph glands being removed (Axillary lymph node clearance)
Description: Surgery to assess or treat lymph nodes under the arm, helping guide breast cancer treatment decisions.

Name: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
Description: Operation in which only the first 1-3 draining lymph nodes are removed to check for cancer spread.

Name: Axillary Lymph node clearance
Description: Operation in which "all" underarm lymph nodes are removed to treat known cancer spread, and assess cancer burden to plan further treatments. This is done when there is confirmed cancer spread in the lymph nodes.

Name:
Neoadjuvant 
Chemotherapy
Patient Facing Questions:
Options 
1) Chemotherapy only
2) Chemotherapy with immunotherapy
3) Chemotherapy with targeted therapy (Herceptin and/or Pertuzumab)
Description: Treatment given before surgery to shrink the cancer and improve surgical and long-term outcomes.

Name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy
Description: Anti-cancer drugs given before surgery to kill cancer cells

Name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with immunotherapy
Description: Chemotherapy combined with immune-boosting treatment, before surgery, to help your body attack cancer cells, usually used in specific breast cancer type (called triple negative cancer).

Name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with targeted therapy
Patient Facing Label: Chemotherapy before surgery with targeted therapy
Description: Chemotherapy combined with drugs targeting specific cancer features or pathways, before surgery, improving response to chemotherapy and reducing recurrence risk, usually used in specific breast cancer type (e.g. blocking growth factor receptors in HER2 +ve cancer)

Name: Neoadjuvant endocrine treatment
Description: Hormone-blocking treatment, given before surgery, to slow growth of cancer if you are temporarily unfit for surgery, or to shrink the cancer if you are unfit for traditional chemotherapy. This can only be used in hormone-sensitive breast cancer.

Name: Survivorship
Description: Patient has completed active treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy) and is now in the survivorship phase. Regular follow-up appointments will continue to monitor for recurrence.

Name: No medication
Description: Patient has completed all treatment and does not require ongoing medication. Regular monitoring and follow-up appointments continue.

Name: Endocrine treatment and/or Zometa
Patient Facing Label: Ongoing Hormone Therapy after Active Treatment
Description: Patient continues on endocrine therapy (hormone tablets) and/or zoledronic acid (Zometa) as part of long-term treatment to reduce recurrence risk.

Name: Further surgery
Patient Facing Questions: Do you need further surgery after your first surgery?
Description: After pathology review of the first surgery, further surgery may be needed if there is suspicion of residual cancer in the breast or in the lymph nodes.

Name: Axilla lymph node clearance
Patient Facing Label: Further Surgery to remove all Lymph Nodes
Patient Facing Questions: Do you need further surgery to remove all lymph nodes (Axillary lymph nodes clearance)
Description: Operation in which "all" underarm lymph nodes are removed to treat known cancer spread, and assess cancer burden to plan further treatments. This is done when there is confirmed cancer spread in the lymph nodes.

Name: Breast margin excision
Patient Facing Label: Further Surgery to remove more Breast Tissue
Patient Facing Questions: Do you need further surgery to remove more breast tissue?
Description: Operation in which breast tissue (suspected to contain residual cancer) is removed.

Name: Completion mastectomy
Patient Facing Label: Further Surgery to remove all Breast tissue
Description: Operation in which all breast tissue is removed, as it is suspected to contain residual cancer.

Name: Adjuvant radiotherapy
Description: Treatment with radiation to the breast (after breast conservation surgery), or to chest wall (after mastectomy, advanced cancer), or to other nodal areas (like supraclavicular or internal mammary areas)

Name: Adjuvant chemotherapy
Description: Systemic administration of medications to kill cancer cells. Chemotherapy may be combined with immunotherapy (for triple negative cancer), or targeted therapy (in HER2 positive cancer), or with zoledronic acid (for women with high risk breast cancer, to reduce risk of bone recurrence).

Name: Adjuvant endocrine therapy
Patient Facing Questions:
Option 1: Hormone Therapy only
Option 2: Hormone Therapy and Zoledronic Acid
Description: Endocrine therapy is indicated in patients with estrogen receptor positive breast cancer. This is typically the last leg of treatment.

Name: Adjuvant endocrine therapy only
Description: Endocrine therapy is indicated in patients with estrogen receptor positive breast cancer.

Name: Adjuvant endocrine therapy and Zoledronic acid
Patient Facing Label: Hormone therapy after Surgery and Zoledronic acid (Zometa) treatment
Description: In postmenopausal women, zoledronic acid is indicated in combination with endocrine therapy to improve survival by inhibiting bone breakdown.

Name: Adjuvant Zoledronic acid (Zometa)
Description: In postmenopausal women, zoledronic acid is indicated to improve survival by inhibiting bone breakdown. Often given in combination with endocrine therapy.
